editorial:
Imagine falling deeply in love only to have a fake friend whisper lies in your ear until you can't trust anyone. That is exactly what happens to Othello, a brave general who marries the sweet Desdemona. While they start off happy, the movie quickly turns into a tense game of lies and tricks. You will feel the pressure build up as Othello is tricked into believing his wife is cheating on him. The vibe is heavy and sad, making you wish you could just yell at the screen and tell him the truth. It is a story about how easy it is for a little bit of doubt to ruin everything.

The acting is the best part here because the emotions feel real and raw. You will love seeing the villain Iago play his games, though he will definitely make you angry. The pacing is steady, but some parts might feel slow if you are not used to old-style talking. If you enjoy heavy dramas, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart when Othello finally gives in to his jealousy and kills Desdemona in their bed. Right after, he finds out that Iago lied about everything and Desdemona was actually innocent. Heartbroken and guilty, Othello kills himself to end his own pain. Iago gets caught and punished for his lies. It is a sad ending because the truth comes out way too late to save anyone.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about betrayal and strong emotions.
